article_title.ru: Прогноз формы шнура и выбор движения дали разные результаты
article_title.en: Cable prediction and action selection favor different information
article_title.ja: ひもの形の予測と動作選択を別々に評価

caption.ru: Инженер в очках и свитере проверяет изображение шнура на компьютере. Две камеры направлены на рабочий стол, роботизированная рука отведена в сторону. Редакционная интерпретация исследования Болонского университета: качество прогноза деформации и выбор полезного действия оценивают раздельно. Люди и оборудование обобщены, а плакат с оптической схемой — условная учебная деталь, не копия исторического плаката. Сцена не воспроизводит точную установку авторов.
caption.en: An engineer wearing glasses and a sweater examines the cable image on a computer. Two cameras face the work surface, with the robot arm parked to one side. An editorial interpretation of the University of Bologna study evaluating deformation prediction and useful action selection separately. The person and equipment are generalized; the optics poster is an illustrative teaching detail, not a reproduction of a historical poster. This is not a reconstruction of the authors’ apparatus.
caption.ja: 眼鏡とセーター姿の技術者が、コンピューターでひもの映像を確認する。二台のカメラが作業面を向き、ロボットアームは横に退避している。変形の予測と動作選択を分けて評価したボローニャ大学の研究を題材にした編集イラスト。人物と装置は一般化した表現で、光学のポスターも説明用の創作であり、歴史的な実物の複製ではない。著者の実験装置を正確に再現した場面ではない。

alt.ru: Чёрно-белая гравюра: один инженер в очках и свитере печатает на клавиатуре, глядя на монитор с изображением изогнутого шнура. Сам шнур с двумя свободными концами лежит на прочном столе. Слева камера закреплена на короткой стойке, сверху вторая камера направлена вниз и закреплена на жёсткой опоре; монитор не перекрывает ей обзор. Справа роботизированная рука с открытым пустым захватом. На стене учебный плакат с линзой и сходящимися лучами, без надписей. Женщины, бумаги и карандаша нет.
alt.en: Black-and-white engraving: one engineer in glasses and a sweater types while looking at a monitor showing the curved cable. The real cable, with two free ends, rests on a sturdy table. A camera stands on a short post at left; a second downward-facing camera is secured to a rigid overhead support with its view clear of the monitor. An articulated robot with an empty open gripper stands at right. A wall teaching poster shows a lens and converging rays without lettering. No woman, paper or pencil.
alt.ja: 白黒の版画。眼鏡とセーター姿の技術者一人が、曲がったひもの映像を見るモニターに向かい、キーボードを操作する。実物のひもは両端が自由な状態で丈夫な台に載る。左のカメラは短い支柱に固定され、上のカメラは頑丈な支持具に付き、モニターに遮られず下向きに撮影する。右には空のつかみ部を開いたロボットアーム。壁の文字のない教材ポスターにはレンズと集まる光線が描かれている。女性、用紙、鉛筆はない。

visual_thesis: Проверка формы шнура после выполненного действия. Камеры наблюдают предмет на плоскости, инженер работает с изображением на компьютере. Это обобщённая редакционная сцена по статье Болонского университета о различии качества прогноза и качества управления; число и размещение камер и учебный плакат не заявляются точными деталями исследовательской установки. Опыты не показывают завязывание узлов или промышленный монтаж.
visual_brief:
Edit the supplied editorial engraving. Preserve the same single cable-shaping robotics story, black ink on pure white, mid-20th-century Soviet scientific engraving language, clear contours, moderate crosshatching, light faces and hands, landscape 16:9. Preserve the pleasant young male engineer's identity, short wavy hair, glasses and crewneck knitted sweater. Preserve the cable lying fully supported in a broad shallow S curve on the sturdy bench, and the simple robot arm fixed to the right side of that bench with its OPEN EMPTY gripper parked safely away from the cable.

Requested changes:
1. REMOVE THE WOMAN COMPLETELY, including all her hands, body, hair and clothing. There must be exactly ONE human: the male engineer. Remove the straight measuring strip she used. Restore clean uninterrupted table and restrained wall where she was. No ghost body parts.
2. Replace the man's PAPER AND PENCIL with a modern desktop computer. No paper or pencil anywhere. A modest flat monitor on a fully connected stable stand is on the bench in the space vacated by the woman, turned toward both the man and the viewer. A keyboard lies flat directly in front of it. The man is actively typing with both hands naturally touching the keys, looking at the monitor rather than at viewer. Repose his arms only as needed to make this plausible, keep his face/hair/glasses/sweater. Place equipment within comfortable arm reach; the keyboard is not under the monitor or another solid. Show on the monitor only ONE large monochrome camera image of the same S-curved cable resting on the table, top-down. This is a camera observation, not a simulation. No UI panels, text, code, charts, buttons, graphs, multiple images or invented numeric results.
3. Add exactly TWO small industrial cameras, each with a clearly visible lens aimed at the cable, NOT aimed at the man. One overhead camera above the cable is on a simple rigid L-shaped support: a vertical post firmly fixed to the back edge of the bench, a short horizontal crossbar visibly connected to it, and a camera securely attached under that bar with lens pointing downward. Second camera on a separate short rigid post bolted to the bench, aimed obliquely at the cable from the far-left/rear edge. Keep the cameras distinct from lights. No tripod legs on the cable, no floating cameras or unsupported brackets. Keep the overhead camera's viewing direction clear. Minimal black signal cables may run attached along the supports toward the computer; no cable dangles into the robot workspace. The experimental S-shaped cable is a separate object and must not be connected to cameras, computer or robot.
4. Add ONE secondary educational wall poster in the upper-left background, in perspective flat against the wall. It depicts a simple vintage scientific illustration of a convex optical lens with rays converging, in black ink on white, without lettering or slogans. It is a generalized teaching poster about camera optics, not a claimed reproduction of an identifiable historic poster. Thin paper edge, no ornate frame, no political symbols. It must remain behind the equipment and not interfere with the man's face or the cameras. No readable text anywhere.

Physical consistency and visual economy: every object on the table supported, monitor stand fully attached, robot links and joints connected, human fingers anatomically plausible and visibly typing, cable has two visible free ends on tabletop. Cameras must have intelligible mounts and line of sight. No extra devices, posters, humans or decorative controls. No colour, sepia, toned paper, grey wash, neon, logos or watermark. Do not create a collage or another story. The scene is a generalized editorial interpretation of checking actual cable shape after a robot movement, not an exact reconstruction of the Bologna research apparatus. Keep enough empty white so this prints clearly at small size.

Final camera line-of-sight correction:
Make one precise mechanical-layout correction to this otherwise approved engraving. Preserve exactly the same male engineer with glasses and sweater typing, two cameras, robot, S-shaped cable on table, optics poster, black ink style, white background and 16:9 framing. No woman, paper or pencil.

CRITICAL: the top-down camera must have an unoccluded view of the physical cable. Currently its optical path is blocked by the computer monitor. Correct their separation:
- Move the monitor about 140 pixels LEFT and make it about 15% smaller, keeping its stand/base fully connected to the bench and its screen image of the same cable. Keep comfortable keyboard and engineer position. The monitor's RIGHTMOST edge must lie LEFT of the overhead camera's vertical optical axis, with a generous visible gap.
- Move the overhead camera box and its downward-pointing lens RIGHT along the existing horizontal support beam, close to the beam's right-hand vertical post but securely mounted. The overhead lens should be approximately above the RIGHT-HAND bend of the real cable. Keep the existing overhead support post solidly fixed to the bench.
- The empty air below that lens, all the way down to the cable, must not contain the monitor, a human, the robot arm or any obstruction. The lens points straight down toward the tabletop cable, not at the monitor. Do not draw a beam or arrow representing this invisible optical path.
- Preserve the second oblique camera and the robot arm at far right. Keep the empty open gripper away from the cable and camera. Preserve the wall poster without words. Do not add objects or people.

This is a layout-only correction for camera line of sight. Keep same scene, same engraving and physical contacts.
